A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AP-Attack, and all 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither contains an appendix. Both reference separate vocabulary supplements that are absent from the supplied PDFs; the available material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-dataset, cross-model and combined-transfer experiments, feature-loss and prompt-template ablations, and qualitative visualizations in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original attack experiments and reports additional defense evaluations, tests on additional target models, and adversarial attribute visualizations.

M1.justification: The five attribute-specific inversion networks, two-stage training procedure, prompt template, generator and losses remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 corrects the swapped visual/text encoder labels to match the existing method description; this does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: v3 retains DukeMTMC, Market, MSMT17 and CUHK03 coverage, adds occluded-person evaluation through PGFA on Occluded-Duke, and introduces defended-system scenarios involving adversarial training, randomization and JPEG processing. These materially broaden the tested conditions. PASS and CLIP-ReID evaluations reuse Market.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same eight competing attacks. The new defense comparison in v3 Table 4 uses a restricted comparison set of MetaAttack, Mis-Ranking and MUAP, without PDCL-Attack or the other generative baselines. No new competing attack algorithm is introduced; PASS, PGFA and CLIP-ReID are target models.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate adversarially trained targets and input defenses, specify JPEG at 60% and BOT(Market), and test PASS, PGFA and CLIP-ReID with mAP and newly reported Rank-1 accuracy. The prompt-template comparison is removed. The retained experiments keep their IDE/DukeMTMC setup, metrics and 8/255 perturbation bound.

E4.justification: v1's six-template sensitivity study and its discussion are removed. v3 adds tests against three defenses and expands Figure 3 from benign attribute interpretation to paired benign/adversarial word clouds examining semantic disruption. The feature-loss ablation in Table 5 and perturbation visualization in Figure 4 remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5 retain their numerical results. New Table 4 reports AP-Attack defense results of 31.1 aAP and 61.1 mDR. New Table 6 reports clean-to-attacked mAP changes of 92.2 to 12.1 for PASS, 37.3 to 4.2 for PGFA, and 89.6 to 32.7 for CLIP-ReID. Figure 3 adds adversarial semantic findings, while five alternative-prompt result pairs disappear. These are added or removed results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), mathematical assumptions and loss definitions are unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs, and v3 introduces none.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same attribute-aware attack contribution, textual-inversion novelty claim and reported 22.9-percentage-point mDR advantage in combined transfer. The additional experiments support the existing central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning effectiveness against defenses, applicability across model paradigms, and disruption of most attribute semantics in the adversarial word clouds. It emphasizes single-dataset training when discussing MetaAttack, but removes the explanation that including 'person' improves attribute learning. The main explanation of advantages over PDCL-Attack remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and configurations for the new evaluations, including the JPEG setting and target-model/dataset pairings. The explicit alternative prompt strings disappear with their ablation. Existing optimizer, learning rate, generator source, PyTorch and RTX3090 disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for JPEG defense, randomization, PGFA and PASS, and adds a single-dataset comparison with MetaAttack. The related-work sections and central positioning against existing VLM-guided attacks otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. Local changes include new Sections 4.4–4.5, removal of the prompt-template discussion, revised captions, corrected encoder labels, updated authors and affiliations, and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Presentation changes concentrate on the experimental pages: the prompt table is replaced by a defense table, Table 6 is added, and Figure 3 gains adversarial word clouds and a revised caption. Existing tables are compacted, Table 5 labels are clarified, and Figure 1 is lightly revised. The overall layout and principal method diagram remain stable.

improvement.justification: The defense tests, additional model paradigms and adversarial word clouds strengthen evidence for practical transferability and semantic disruption, while the code link improves access information. These gains are tempered by losing the prompt-sensitivity study and limitations in the new evidence: Table 6 lacks competing attacks, and Table 4 reports benign aAP of 80.0 although its three entries average 79.3. The net improvement is useful but limited.
